annotations.text:
Proposal for Models / Performance / Settings. Header, Editor and Jobs untouched.

Same type ramp, same violet, same control heights — nothing here needs a new design system.

Three changes are shared across all three pages:

1. The page ground drops one step (light 0.98 → 0.965 L, dark 0.13 → 0.115) so cards read as a raised surface instead of a hairline outline. This is the one change that also touches Editor and Jobs — two lines in index.css, and it helps both.

2. Badges become theme-aware: dark ink on a light tint in light mode, the reverse in dark. The current bg-*-500/20 + text-*-400 pairing is dark-only, and washes out on white.

3. One page-header pattern: title, one subtitle line, 24px. Today all three pages do this differently.

Performance

• Status is stated once beside the title. Was LIVE ×7 plus 'telemetry available' ×6.
• All four tiles now lead with a percentage, so they are comparable; bytes move to the sub-line. Each carries a sparkline of the same series the chart below plots.
• The two 500px donuts become two stacked bars in one 208px card — same three numbers each, a quarter of the space, and RAM vs VRAM now sit side by side. Each bar uses its own metric's colour, so a RAM bar is no longer drawn in the CPU's purple.
• The trend chart gets a legend. Four unlabelled lines was the worst readability problem on the page.

The whole page now fits 900px without scrolling — it needed 1166 before.

Models

• Filter bar is one row of 36px controls in two segmented groups — was 36 / 32 / 36 with no grouping and a barely-visible selected state.
• Model name is now mono (it is an identifier); the filename drops to a quiet footer line.
• Type carries the only colour, and it is the SAME accent as that node in the Editor palette (orange = Super Resolution, cyan = Frame Interpolation). 4x / FP16 become neutral spec chips.
• Card gets a spine: name → type → description → rule → Range / Input → filename.

Model detail — this is where clicking a card goes.

Everything on this board is read out of the real the_database_AnimeJaNaiV3L1_sharp_HD_x2_fp16_op17.onnx: 55 ops, opset 17, IR 8, pytorch 2.1.2, float16 [?, 3, ?, ?] in and out. The architecture drawn is the actual one — SRVGGNetCompact: Conv 3→24 + PRelu, then Conv 24→24 + PRelu eight more times, Conv 24→12, DepthToSpace blocksize 2 CRD, joined by Add with a nearest-neighbour Resize of the input, then Clip.

What changed from the modal:
• A full-width surface instead of a 768px dialog. The graph is the reason you opened this.
• No tabs. Metadata and the I/O schema live in the rail and stay on screen — the graph IS the schema, so splitting them across tabs was fighting itself.
• Left-to-right, like the Editor. The current one is top-to-bottom, so the app has two graphs that read in different directions.
• The 32 Constant nodes are hidden. They are weights, not structure, and they were 58% of the boxes.
• The repeated Conv → PRelu run collapses to one block with a ×8 chip.
• Operators is the other half: op counts by type, and the 23-op sequence. The current view cannot answer what is in this model at all.

Settings — rebuilt at Controller density.

Borrowed from controller-web: the 168px section nav beside a bordered content column, section = 13px heading + hairline + grid, 32px fields with 11px labels and mono values on a recessed ground, and the save bar pinned to the foot of the route.

What that buys: numeric values stop getting 432px inputs, so Session fits on one row and Storage puts all four paths on one. The page went 1546px → 1383px → 778px, and now fits on screen with room to spare.

Still fixed from the current build: no stretch holes, footer aligned, one checkbox style, one input radius, human labels with the config key beside them, Server as read-only text rather than 40%-opacity disabled inputs, and Access protection split into Password and Session.

Model detail as it is today — and this one is not a drawing. The 57 boxes are placed by running the app’s own buildOnnxGraph + dagre over the real AnimeJaNai .onnx file, at the zoom React Flow actually settles on.

Three things fall out of that:

1. The layout is 2960 × 2816px. fitView asks for zoom 0.136 to fit it in the 720 × 420 box; React Flow’s default minZoom is 0.5, so it clamps. You land on 49% of the width and can never zoom out far enough — the fit-view button cannot fit the view.

2. There are no edges. OnnxOpNode and OnnxIONode render plain divs with no <Handle>, and getEdgePosition returns null without handle bounds, so all 57 edges are dropped (console error 008). The graph is 57 disconnected boxes.

3. 32 of the 55 nodes are Constant — the weights. The actual architecture is the other 23.

Also: RIFE v4.26 has 636 ops and the tab refuses to draw anything over 500, so the interpolation half of the product has no graph at all. And Parameters reads 0 because param_count sums initializers, of which this model has none — its 44,940 weights are Constant nodes.
